title: FOX software matches or beats manual cochlear-implant fitting in a randomized crossover trial of 24 patients in Brussels
summary: In a randomized crossover trial in Brussels, newly implanted patients fitted with the FOX software understood speech better at 3 and 12 months, and all manual-arm patients kept the FOX map.
account: Two 2019 case studies from the Saint-Luc group in Brussels reported improved word recognition with AI suggestions in one of two adults. Two US studies followed, by authors outside the Saint-Luc and Eargroup teams. Waltzman and Kelsall (2020) reported that FOX maps matched clinician maps on average in 55 experienced adults. Zwolan and colleagues (2021), two of them Cochlear Americas staff, reported scores similar to traditional programming in 31 newly implanted patients, with 43% fewer programming appointments. They state that Otoconsult developed FOX. Wathour et al. (Ear and Hearing, published online 21 December 2022) then ran a one-year randomized crossover trial. It enrolled 24 newly implanted cochlear-implant patients at Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels. It compared manual fitting with the Fitting to Outcome eXpert (FOX). From 3 months the FOX group showed less variability and better speech intelligibility in quiet and in noise. At 3 months its median phoneme scores were 50%, 70% and 50% at 55, 70 and 85 dB SPL, against 45%, 50% and 40% in the manual group. After crossover, 100% of the manual group kept the FOX map and 82% performed better with it. Of the FOX group, 63% preferred their manual map for comfort. A companion study (Otology & Neurotology, 18 January 2023) gave 47 experienced users a FOX map. It found median improvements of 10 dB at 6,000 Hz and of 10% in phonemic discrimination and speech scores after 15 days of take-home use. The two US studies found results similar to those in Brussels. P. J. Govaerts co-authored all three Saint-Luc papers. The cited sources do not establish whether any author is affiliated with Otoconsult. In November 2025 Otoconsult's site described FOX as an outcome-based application assisting audiologists and AI-FOX as the successor of a deterministic first-generation tool.

data.answer:
In a Brussels crossover RCT, newly implanted patients fitted with FOX had better speech intelligibility at 3 and 12 months; all manual-arm patients kept the FOX map; 47 experienced users improved.

The small crossover trial and companion studies need assessment of allocation, carryover, missing results, and author ties to Otoconsult. Better speech scores did not mean universal comfort preference: 63% of the FOX group preferred its manual map. Long-term everyday benefit is unmeasured here.

fields.summary: In a randomized crossover trial in Brussels, newly implanted patients fitted with the FOX software understood speech better at 3 and 12 months, and all manual-arm patients kept the FOX map.
fields.account: Two 2019 case studies from the Saint-Luc group in Brussels reported improved word recognition with AI suggestions in one of two adults. Two US studies followed, by authors outside the Saint-Luc and Eargroup teams. Waltzman and Kelsall (2020) reported that FOX maps matched clinician maps on average in 55 experienced adults. Zwolan and colleagues (2021), two of them Cochlear Americas staff, reported scores similar to traditional programming in 31 newly implanted patients, with 43% fewer programming appointments. They state that Otoconsult developed FOX. Wathour et al. (Ear and Hearing, published online 21 December 2022) then ran a one-year randomized crossover trial. It enrolled 24 newly implanted cochlear-implant patients at Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels. It compared manual fitting with the Fitting to Outcome eXpert (FOX). From 3 months the FOX group showed less variability and better speech intelligibility in quiet and in noise. At 3 months its median phoneme scores were 50%, 70% and 50% at 55, 70 and 85 dB SPL, against 45%, 50% and 40% in the manual group. After crossover, 100% of the manual group kept the FOX map and 82% performed better with it. Of the FOX group, 63% preferred their manual map for comfort. A companion study (Otology & Neurotology, 18 January 2023) gave 47 experienced users a FOX map. It found median improvements of 10 dB at 6,000 Hz and of 10% in phonemic discrimination and speech scores after 15 days of take-home use. The two US studies found results similar to those in Brussels. P. J. Govaerts co-authored all three Saint-Luc papers. The cited sources do not establish whether any author is affiliated with Otoconsult. In November 2025 Otoconsult's site described FOX as an outcome-based application assisting audiologists and AI-FOX as the successor of a deterministic first-generation tool.
